Method of Attack: Delivered as malware in disk image file formats (.ISO and DAA) acting as archive-like containers to conceal executables; Remote Access Tools (RATs) and information stealers delivered via malicious ISO and DAA disk image files; Malicious ISO files disguised as innocent files (e.g., fake FedEx shipment email with ISO appearing as PDF); DAA images containing single executable with .COM or .EXE extension (Remcos RAT v2.5.0 Pro); Use of disk image formats to slip past antivirus and secure email gateways
Attack Vector: Email attachments with malicious disk image files (.ISO, .DAA); Phishing emails (e.g., fake FedEx shipment, invoice-themed emails); Malicious ISO files mounted by double-clicking in Windows; Targeted attacks using DAA images requiring specialized mounting software
Indicators of Compromise: Malicious ISO file linked in phishing email pretending to be PDF; Executable for NanoCore RAT inside ISO; DAA images containing Remcos RAT v2.5.0 Pro executables with .COM or .EXE extensions; 18 out of 70 antivirus engines on VirusTotal flagged the malicious ISO at time of discovery
